headword: {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}
reading: きんろうかんしゃのひ

definitions.explanation: A Japanese national holiday on November 23 for honoring work and production and for people to thank one another. It continues the old harvest festival {新嘗祭|にいなめさい}, at which the emperor offers the new rice to the gods.

examples.japanese: {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{祝日|しゅくじつ}→祝日：07588_shukujitsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Labor Thanksgiving Day is a national holiday.

examples.japanese: {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{両親|りょうしん}→両親：00806_ryoushin⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦プレゼント→プレゼント：01791_purezento⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}った→贈る：09862_okuru⟧。
examples.english: I gave my parents a present on Labor Thanksgiving Day.

examples.japanese: {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{近|ちか}づく→近づく：01958_chikazuku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{小学校|しょうがっこう}→小学校：01055_shougakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{礼|れい}→お礼：01359_orei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: As Labor Thanksgiving Day approaches, elementary schools sometimes have children write thank-you letters to working people.

notes:
{勤労|きんろう} (work, labor) + ⟦{感謝|かんしゃ}→感謝：00181_kansha⟧ (thanks) + ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧ (day). One of Japan's national holidays (⟦{国民|こくみん}の{祝日|しゅくじつ}→国民の祝日：22469_kokuminnoshukujitsu⟧), fixed on November 23 since 1948.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Before 1948 the same day was {新嘗祭|にいなめさい}, the imperial harvest festival, which is still held privately at the palace and at shrines. Children often mark the day by thanking parents, police officers, or other workers.
